Subject: Security exhibit + SOC 2 evidence cadence for Atlas Health

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Atlas is asking for two items to move the order form forward: a security exhibit we can attach to the MSA that includes SOC 2 language and a clear evidence cadence for periodic requests (SOC 2 reports, penetration test reports, and ad-hoc audit evidence).

Specifically, could you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report annually and along what timing (fiscal vs calendar).
- Pen test frequency and whether Atlas can request a time-boxed access window for our vendor during audits.
- Typical evidence turnaround time (e.g., 5 business days for logs, 10 for configuration artifacts).
- Any redlineable clauses on audit rights / on-site access / liability that we should expect in the order form amendment.

We need a short summary for our security intake and a proposed cadence so we can share with legal. Appreciate a reply this week if possible — procurement is aiming to finish commercial terms by end of month.

Thanks,
Claire Rhodes
Director, Vendor Security
Atlas Health

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together a short package (attached): a draft security exhibit aligned to our standard MSA language and an evidence checklist that maps artifacts to expected SLAs. High level answers below; detailed redlines from legal/security are cc'd.

- SOC 2: Redwood provides an annual SOC 2 Type II report on a calendar-year basis. We make the report available on request to customers with a signed NDA; typical turnaround for providing a copy is 3 business days once the request is approved by our compliance team.
- Pen tests: External pen test performed annually, with our vendor report shared under NDA. For customer-directed penetration testing, we offer a supervised, time-boxed access window (up to 72 hours) coordinated through our security ops team. We require 10 business days' advance notice and a scoped statement of work.
- Evidence cadence & SLAs: We propose the following: SOC 2 report (annual, 3 BD turnaround on request), configuration snapshots (10 BD), audit logs (5 BD for aggregated logs, 10 BD for raw logs), and limited end-point evidence (14 BD). Emergency escalations can be handled faster per mutual agreement.
- Audit rights redlines we expect: request-to-audit process, data minimization for shared artifacts, indemnity carveouts related to customer misuse, and limited on-site access language (we prefer remote evidence review; on-site only for enterprise and with 30 BD notice).

Next steps: Karthik has suggested a few specific MSD/order form edits — Karthik + Monica, can you review the attached exhibit and checklist and flag the high-risk ask items? Claire, if those high-risk items are acceptable we can prepare an order form amendment and route via DocuSign.

Attachments:
- redwood-security-exhibit-draft-v1.pdf (security exhibit with SOC2 & pen-test language)
- atlas-evidence-checklist-2027.xlsx (artifact -> SLA mapping)

Claire / team — quick legal redlines and clarifying Qs inline. I pasted the key points below to keep the thread digestible.

1) SOC 2 report access: we can provide the report under NDA. Legal prefers language that limits redistribution and requires certified receipt. Proposed clause: "Customer may request Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report subject to execution of a mutually acceptable nondisclosure agreement; Customer may not reproduce or distribute the report outside of its internal compliance team."

2) Pen test windows & scopes: Redwood will not accept unsupervised external testing. For customer-requested tests, we require: (i) a scoped test plan; (ii) a point of contact; (iii) adherence to our acceptable testing hours; (iv) indemnity for any damage caused by the test beyond agreed scope. Please confirm Atlas can accept those constraints.

3) Audit rights / on-site access: we are proposing remote evidence review as the default. On-site inspections escalate to an executive approval path and require a separate professional services engagement. This avoids operational risk for our hosted environment.

4) Evidence turnaround SLAs: the draft spreadsheet Jonas attached is reasonable. Legal asks that we keep response times as "best efforts" for certain privileged artifacts and reserve concrete SLAs for logs and configuration that are produced by automated systems.

Claire — if Atlas can accept the redistribution and supervised-testing constraints, we can mark the exhibit as "redline-ready" and I will prepare a clean tracked-order form amendment for signature. If Atlas needs broader audit rights, please flag the specific clauses so we can escalate internally to execs for approval.

-Karthik
